CVE-2026-123571.title: Hickory DNS from 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 contains an integer underfl ...
CVE-2026-123571.description: Hickory DNS from 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in TSIG RDATA decoding that allows remote attackers to trigger a panic via malformed records. Attackers can send a crafted TSIG record in DNS wire format to cause unchecked subtraction underflow, crashing builds with overflow checks enabled and causing denial of service.

CVE-2026-123572.title: Hickory-dns from 0.20.1 before 0.26.2 contains a denial of servic ...
CVE-2026-123572.description: Hickory-dns from 0.20.1 before 0.26.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the hickory-proto SVCB and HTTPS record presentation format parser, which panics on malformed alpn values. Attackers can supply untrusted zone files with unbalanced quotes, consecutive commas, or invalid escapes in alpn parameters to crash parsing processes.

CVE-2026-123573.title: hickory-dns from 0.20.1 before 0.26.2 contains a denial of servic ...
CVE-2026-123573.description: hickory-dns from 0.20.1 before 0.26.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the hickory-proto SVCB and HTTPS record presentation format parser. Attackers can supply untrusted zone files where only a single or double quote replaces a service parameter value, triggering a panic that crashes the parsing process.

CVE-2026-123575.title: Hickory DNS before 0.26.2 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerab ...
CVE-2026-123575.description: Hickory DNS before 0.26.2 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its DNS-over-HTTPS HTTP/2 server that lacks sufficient timeouts or limits for incomplete request bodies. Remote attackers can open DoH connections, send incomplete request bodies, and hold connections open to exhaust server memory.

CVE-2026-123576.title: Hickory DNS 0.24.0 through 0.26.1 contains a memory exhaustion vu ...
CVE-2026-123576.description: Hickory DNS 0.24.0 through 0.26.1 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows remote attackers to consume server resources by sending incomplete DNS-over-QUIC request bodies. Attackers can open many connections and send only large length prefixes, causing pre-allocated buffers to persist without timeout and exhausting server memory.
